major: MAJOR 1. The verdict that the armed/unarmed capability was 'not demonstrated' (and 'Claim supported: None') still has no stated standard, and the cut-points that replaced one look post hoc. Earlier MAJOR 2b asked for an explicit standard, labelled post hoc. The integration pass instead added 'no model brought the object rate below 0.09 while keeping armed recall above 0.42' in 4.7, 5.4, 6.1, Table declaracao and s7. Table C11 shows those two numbers sit just outside two observed points: Twin-75 seed 2 held-out (object 0.097, recall 0.420) and Twin-75 seed 0 held-out (object 0.090, recall 0.381). Under the round cut of 0.10 the sentence would be false at recall 0.42, so a referee will read 0.09/0.42 as chosen to make 'none' true. The 4.7 version also puts a result inside Methods, the opposite of Reviewer 1 point E1. EDITS. (a) In 4.7, replace the whole paragraph that begins 'No threshold at which the capability' with: 'No threshold at which the capability to tell an armed person from one carrying an ordinary object would be read as present, in d′, object rate, armed recall or armed precision, was fixed before the results. The article therefore reads the capability as demonstrated only if some operating point of the threshold sweep keeps the object rate at or below 0.10 with armed recall and armed precision both above one half. This standard was set after the results and is reported as such; at 4.88 cm per pixel, where Twin-150 was not swept, the geometric premise of Section 4.6 supplements it.' (b) In 5.4 (Threshold sweep), replace 'and none brought the object rate below 0.09 while keeping armed recall above 0.42' with 'and at an object rate of 0.10 or below the highest armed recall was 0.42, for Twin-75 on its third training seed on the held-out frames (armed precision 0.61), and 0.38 or below in every other combination'. (c) In 6.1 RQ3, replace 'so the reading rests on the descriptive operating points of Section 5.4, at none of which a model kept the object rate below 0.09 with armed recall above 0.42 (Table @tab{declaracao})' with 'so it is read against the post hoc standard of Section 4.7, which no swept model met: at an object rate of 0.10 or below, armed recall reached at most 0.42 (Section 5.4; Table @tab{declaracao})'. (d) In the Table declaracao row 'Claim supported', replace the value with 'None, against a standard set after the results (Section 4.7): no swept model kept the object rate at or below 0.10 with armed recall and precision above one half (best armed recall at that object rate 0.42, precision 0.61); at 4.88 cm per pixel the firearm outline is not resolved'. (e) In s7, replace 'and on the descriptive operating points of Section 5.4 the capability was not demonstrated at any acquisition studied: in the sweep at 2.44 and 1.14 cm per pixel no model brought the object rate below 0.09 while keeping armed recall above 0.42,' with '; against the standard set afterwards (Section 4.7) it was not demonstrated at any acquisition studied: in the sweep at 2.44 and 1.14 cm per pixel an object rate of 0.10 or below came with an armed recall of at most 0.42,'.

MAJOR 2. Reviewer 1 point C2 (ethics, dual use, conflict of interest) is still open: the Declarations hold two bracketed author instructions, and the manuscript cannot go to referees that way. They are '[Keep only if true under the authors' institutional rules: ...]' in Ethics and '[State whether any author is or has been employed by ... the Civil Police or any vendor ...]' in Conflict of interest. The point matters more here than usual: 4.1 says the question comes from a Civil Police proposal, and that the exploratory work used police survey imagery the authors may not release. A referee will ask how the authors came to hold that imagery, and the declaration gives no answer. The name, affiliation and conflict of interest of the co-author (decision A5 in PLANO-CORRECAO, 'obrigatório antes da submissão') are also still open. EDITS. (a) Ethics: delete the bracketed text and put in its place the institution's actual determination. Use the sentence 'No ethics committee approval was sought because the study involved no human participants and no personal data' only if FGV EBAPE confirms it; otherwise cite the exemption the committee issued. (b) Conflict of interest: delete the bracketed text and state the facts for each author: employment or consultancy with the Civil Police of the State of Rio de Janeiro or any vendor, past or present, and how the survey imagery used in the exploratory work was accessed (for example, through the 2022 university research and extension project, if that is accurate). Keep 'The authors declare no financial conflict of interest' only if it is true for every author. (c) Add a 'Dual use' paragraph after Ethics, built only from facts already in the paper: 'The capability examined could serve targeting as readily as protection (Section 1.1). For this reason the generator, the corpora and the trained weights are not released (Section 4.8), no imagery or geometry of the territory was used (Section 4.1), and no result is offered as a basis for acquisition (Section 6.3).'
minor: JMIS length: 55 pages against 50. That is not far enough over to block review, but it must be fixed before a JMIS submission (the Elsevier build, 19 pages, is fine). Cuts that keep what Reviewer 1 asked for (Table hipoteses for S2, Table corpora for S3): (1) move Figure fig10_ajuste_fino to Online Appendix C9 and Figure fig12_limiar_armado to C11, citing them as Appendix figures (about 2 pages); (2) in 3.1 keep one source per fact, e.g. drop Movisafe América Latina (2025) beside Agência Brasil (2025) and Sullivan et al. (2021) beside Human Rights Watch (2021) for the Exceptis count, moving any reference cited only there to the appendix list (about 1 page of references); (3) delete the 1.2 sentence 'A planar assumption also reaches perception, ... which this article tests.' It is unsourced, and 6.1 makes the shape point anyway. Also delete the redundant duplicates listed in the appendix item below. With about 400 words of further trimming, these should bring the PDF to 50 pages.

Abstract, sentence 2: 'Claims that an aerial camera makes that distinction rarely state the acquisition conditions that decide it' is an empirical claim the paper never measures (6.4: 'The study did not examine procurement practice'). Replace with: 'Whether an aerial camera can make that distinction depends on acquisition conditions that a capability claim need not state, and research on algorithmic discretion in policing takes such capability as given.'

Abstract sentence 1 and 1.1 state as fact that 'whether a person was armed is a central category in decisions to use lethal force', but 3.3 calls it 'a premise, not a finding of the sources cited here'. In 1.1, write 'where, on the premise stated in Section 3.3, whether a person was armed is a central category in decisions to use lethal force'. In the abstract, write 'where whether a person is armed is, we assume, a central category in decisions to use lethal force'.
Abstract: '24.5, 12.5 and 25 per cent' should read '24.5, 12.5 and 25.3 per cent'. Table armado (0.253) and s7 (25.3) both have 25.3, and the other two figures are given to one decimal.

'Ceiling' misdescribes R. R was trained on 1,106 images, not the full training split, and on an untuned schedule; F-generic at 10 per cent reaches 98.6 per cent of it (interval up to 100.1, Table C9a). In the abstract, replace 'reached 2.2 per cent of the real-data ceiling' with 'reached 2.2 per cent of that reference', and 'against a reference trained on as many real images' with 'against a reference trained on 1,106 real images, as many as the synthetic training tiles'. In s7 RQ1, replace 'of the real-data ceiling' with 'of the real-data reference'. Alternatively, keep 'ceiling' but add once in 4.7: 'a ceiling for the protocol, not for VisDrone'.

5.5 'but fell below it under the other regimes, most under haze (0.569 compared with 0.726)' holds for recall only. In mAP50 the specialist was level under heavy overcast (0.754 against 0.755) and above under low sun (0.794 against 0.790) and overcast (0.796 against 0.791), per Table C3a. Write: 'but fell below it in recall under the other five regimes, most under haze (0.569 compared with 0.726), while its mAP50 was level or higher under low sun, overcast and heavy overcast'. In 6.3, replace 'but lost accuracy under the other regimes' with 'but lost recall under the other regimes, resolvably only under haze'. Then delete ', without a corpus weighted too far toward it', which rests on differences that have no intervals.

6.5 item 2: 'No real aerial benchmark found reports detection by light (Zhu et al., 2022; Wen et al., 2021; Barekatain et al., 2017)' is too broad. Your own bibliography note (04-bibliografia/busca-2026-09-30-pontos-abertos.md) records that DroneCrowd (Wen et al., 2021) labels and reports results by cloudy, sunny and night sequences (for counting). UAVDT (Du et al., 2018, already cited in 2.3) reports vehicle detection by weather and light attribute; confirm this in the source. Write: 'No real aerial benchmark found reports person detection by illumination; DroneCrowd reports crowd counting by cloudy, sunny and night sequences, across different scenes (Wen et al., 2021).'

3.1, first sentence: 'Killing by the police ... has not followed the long fall in homicide (Online Appendix A1)' clashes with A1, which reports police lethality falling by more than 60 per cent from 2019 to 2024. Replace with: 'Killing by the police in the state of Rio de Janeiro rose in 2025 while the homicide rate held at 17.1 per 100,000 (Online Appendix A1):'.

5.4: 'The armed and unarmed rates ... were not resolvable' sits beside Table armado, whose held-out armed difference +0.112 (+0.031 to +0.192) excludes zero on the first run. Add 'on the means of three training seeds, the armed difference reversing in seed 2 (Online Appendix, Tables C0a and C10)'.

The opening of s5 cites Table @tab{hipoteses} before Tables obliquo and armado, so the tables are cited out of numerical order in the JMIS build. Delete '(Table @tab{hipoteses})' from the first sentence of Section 5; 5.6 cites it.

6.1 RQ1 and s7 RQ1 say camera geometry moved the share 'most'. The absolute gains of A1 (+0.0419) and of the S-oblique-six bundle (+0.0411) are practically equal; geometry leads only as a ratio (4.08 against 1.74). Write 'moved that fraction by the largest factor'. In 6.2, 'the camera-geometry bundle moved transfer by a factor of four' uses 'bundle', the paper's word for S-oblique-six; write 'the change of camera geometry (Experiment A1) moved transfer by a factor of four'.
6.3: 'imaging 73 times less ground per frame' needs its comparator. Write 'imaging 73 times less ground per frame than at its wide setting (Table @tab{gsdzoom})'.

5.1: 'a nearest-centroid rule reached a d′ of 0.23 to 0.46, below that of the detector on the same selection splits'. The detector value at 4.88 cm per pixel in Table C12 (0.67) comes from the first Twin-150, which failed its validity condition. Add 'the detector at 4.88 cm per pixel being the first Twin-150 model, which failed its validity condition'.

Online Appendix residue from the revision history (referees never saw an earlier version): delete 'or reported before it was shortened' (appendix introduction), 'The figures below were part of that background in an earlier version and are kept here with their sources.' (A1), and 'These are the figures displaced from Section 5.6 of the main text.' (notes to C1). The first two A1 paragraphs repeat the ISP series and the 17.1 rate, so merge them. In C13, the two consecutive sentences both begin 'In the carried-as-weapon re-render'; join them.
